text:
Ladybird / lady beetles (various species) -- a beneficial insect group.

Description: adult colour and pattern vary widely between species (solid red, spotted, striped, or black); adults are round to oval and roughly 4-8 mm long. Larvae look quite different from the adults -- elongated and spiny -- and are easy to mistake for a pest if not recognised.

Role: both larval and adult stages feed on aphids, making this one of the most important beneficial insect groups for aphid control; larvae in particular are voracious predators and are also known to feed on the eggs of pest species such as Helicoverpa (corn earworm). Conserving ladybird populations (for example by minimising unnecessary insecticide use) is an important part of an IPM strategy for corn.
